description: REQ-101's headline EARS behavior is liveness-based staleness ('WHILE a lock holder is still actively executing its critical section, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT allow any other caller to acquire the same lock key, regardless of how much wall-clock time has elapsed'), concretely tested by lock.test.mjs's integration-level test named '\u2605GAP 1\u2605 a live holder's lock is NEVER stolen while it's still working past staleMs (heartbeat keeps it alive)' (skills/economy/gig/__tests__/lock.test.mjs:24-61). None of the 8 CRIT items name this test (or PROP-101a specifically) as a required-present-by-name check the way CRIT-002 explicitly names the Tier-2 atomicity test ('\u2605PROP-101c (Tier 2, atomicity)\u2605') and CRIT-004 explicitly names \u2605FINDING 1\u2605/\u2605FINDING 2\u2605/\u2605FINDING 3\u2605. CRIT-001's passThreshold only requires (a) the structural isLockStale extraction and (b) that 'lock.test.mjs's PROP-101a/b/c(purity-half)/d tests import and exercise isLockStale directly' -- it points to the generic '8/8 lock.test.mjs PASS' log line as supporting evidence rather than making the heartbeat-liveness test itself a named FAIL trigger. CRIT-004's aggregate 'exactly 48/48' count across the whole gig test suite would catch an outright test REMOVAL, but a future edit that silently renamed or replaced \u2605GAP 1\u2605 with a materially weaker test (e.g., one that only checks a single heartbeat tick instead of the full 3x-staleMs long-running scenario) while keeping the total test count at 48 would not trip any of CRIT-001/002/004's named-test FAIL conditions. REQ-101's own liveness scenario is the entire reason the round-3 heartbeat fix exists (see gig/lib/lock.mjs:15-22's header comment on the real double-pay drain this was built to close) -- it deserves the same explicit by-name protection CRIT-002 gives the atomicity test.

recommendation: Add an explicit FAIL trigger to CRIT-001 (or a new CRIT) requiring the adversary to confirm the '\u2605GAP 1\u2605' heartbeat-liveness test is present BY NAME and passes when independently re-run, mirroring CRIT-002's treatment of the atomicity test.
